llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions broadly match a local sandboxing/orchestration tool, but important pieces are omitted from the provided files (notably the micro-VM/container orchestration code) and a few operational details could expose host secrets or mounts if misused — review those parts before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (pre-install sandboxing) align with required binaries (docker, python3) and included scripts (obfuscator, entropy gate, behavioral audit, output filter). No unrelated cloud credentials or surprising dependencies are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the visible orchestrator scripts describe a deterministic, local 5-layer pipeline and explicitly avoid network I/O and host env leakage. However several important runtime behaviors depend on scripts that were truncated/omitted here (microvm_orchestrator.py and other truncated files). Those are the components that actually run the untrusted code inside containers/micro-VMs and decide volume mounts, Docker run flags, seccomp enforcement, and trace collection. Without reviewing them, you cannot confirm there are no unintended host mounts, privileged flags, or external endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is present (instruction-only + bundled scripts). Dockerfile uses standard images (python:3.11-slim and gcr.io/distroless) which are expected and reasonable. One operational caveat: building the sandbox image will fetch base images (network) unless already cached — SKILL.md correctly says runtime uses --network=none but initial docker build may require network access.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables and the orchestrator implements a whitelist (_build_safe_env) to avoid passing host secrets to subprocesses. This is proportionate. That said, earlier README text concedes a past leak and the protection depends on every subprocess invocation using the sanitized environment; you should verify the orchestration code (especially Docker invocation in microvm_orchestrator.py) does not pass the full host env or mount files that expose secrets.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request forced always-on presence and is user-invocable. Docker mode is designed to run non-root; Firecracker micro-VM mode requires root (documented). There is no sign the skill modifies other skills' configs or requests persistent system-wide privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package is largely coherent with its stated purpose (local sandboxing and forensic audit). Before you install or run it: 1) Review the full microvm_orchestrator.py and any truncated scripts to confirm Docker run commands do not mount sensitive host paths, do not pass the full host environment, and use the documented seccomp profile and --network=none. 2) Confirm how Docker images are built on your machine (building the image pulls base images from the network unless already cached). 3) Audit any code paths that invoke subprocesses to ensure the whitelist environment is actually used for Docker runs. 4) If you intend to use the Firecracker mode, expect it requires root and extra kernel privileges — only enable that on a controlled host. Finally, test Black-Fortress with benign sample code first and run it on an isolated host or VM until you’ve validated its behavior.
